lines.en: Two days had passed since the ‘Great Apocalypse Scenario’ ended.
During those two days, the lingering 98th scenario had ended as well.
[Scenario 98 ― ‘Candidate Selection War’ has ended automatically.]
[No one challenged your nebula.]
[Current number of victories: 1]
[Your rewards are currently under review.]
[Your rewards are being discussed in conjunction with the clearing of the ‘Great Apocalypse Scenario’.]

Perhaps it was only natural. While the nebulae fought one another, we had overcome the ‘Great Apocalypse Scenario’. We had fought those unfathomable ‘Outer Gods’ and protected Earth. All with the power of a single nebula.
[A considerable number of constellations respect you and your nebula.]
[The renown of the nebula <Kim Dokja’s Company> spreads throughout the <Star Stream>!]
[Every constellation in the final scenario knows your nebula.]
[Every constellation in the final scenario is curious about your ‘Conclusion’.]
Now, there was no one in this <Star Stream> who did not know us.
―Representative-nim! Representative Kim Dokja-nim! Please give us a comment!
A loudspeaker blared from beyond the [Industrial Complex].

Whether I switched on a hologram panel or a television, wherever I went, people were talking about us. Every broadcaster, terrestrial and cable alike, was showing live footage of the grounds in front of the [Industrial Complex].
Interviews with members of our Industrial Complex were playing on repeat, too.
―‘Judge of Destruction’-nim! As for <Kim Dokja’s Company>’s plans for the future······.
―Please just use my name in public. Han Sooyoung likes that sort of thing, but I don’t.
―Jung Heewon, do you want to die?
······I had lost count of how many times I’d heard that ‘Do you want to die?’
―The real power behind Kim Dokja’s Company, ‘Black Flames Demon Ruler Han Sooyoung’. It turns out she was a famous author before the apocalypse······.
Reading the caption [A genius author’s insight will crack the final scenario!], I felt anew just how far I had come.
―We understand that your representative became a ‘Myth-grade constellation’ when he defeated the ‘Midday Sun’. Does Korea now have a ‘Myth-grade constellation’ taking an active role?
―Incarnations are debating the footage from the end of this battle. Just what were those ‘Outer Gods’?
―Why did Representative Kim Dokja suddenly turn blond?

Our battles had been broadcast throughout Earth as well as the <Star Stream>. From Yoo Joonghyuk driving back ‘Ra’ to our confrontation with the tidal wave of lava created by the Outer Gods of the 999th round.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ is proud.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ holds his head high.]
[The constellation ‘Most Ancient Liberator’ twitches his lips.]
And invariably, each of those scenes was followed by an interview.
―You see, I saw his potential back when he worked at the company. Hm? What sort of new employee clocks out right on time before anyone else, from his very first day······?
······Department Head Han Myungoh. I distinctly remembered telling him not to give interviews.
Beaming, Han Myungoh held his daughter’s hand tightly in his left hand. Fortunately, he seemed to have rescued her safely.
―He was just an ordinary guy. You know the type. There’s always someone like him in every class.
As time passed, people claiming to have been my classmates began to appear, too.
So some of them were still alive, I thought.
Faces whose names I could no longer remember.
―Kind, quiet, liked reading······.
The description wasn’t exactly wrong, but it wasn’t right, either.
There were convenient words in this world, and words that explained nothing precisely because they were so convenient.
After spouting platitudes for quite some time, my former classmate stammered and backed away, perhaps uncomfortable with the camera. There must have been nothing left to say.
―On Earth’s savior, the ‘Demon King of Salvation’.
The next program, accompanied by mournful music, was an entire documentary special.
[The constellation ‘Goryeo’s First Sword’ nods.]
[The constellation ‘Maritime War God’ is proud of you.]
Watching the footage, I thought about the days before the apocalypse. The things I had dreamed of, the things I had believed were important.
It felt terribly strange that all those days had already become distant memories.
Of course, not everything felt unfamiliar.
―Overcoming a painful childhood scarred by domestic violence······.
Someone switched off the television with a click.
“Dokja.”
My mother stood at the entrance to the sitting room.
I gave her a small smile.
“You’re here.”
My mother nodded. The silence filling the sitting room. For a while, we looked at the switched-off television in that silence. My mother and I were reflected in its black screen.
A faint scent of perfume brushed my nose, and suddenly I felt strange.
Once, she had been the one person in the world I could not understand.
Yet now, even without using [Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint], I could tell what she was thinking.
“I’m fine. Don’t worry.”
I heard a faint sigh.
“I’m sorry.”
“This isn’t your fault, Mother.”
“This time······.”
“You’ve had a lot of interview requests, haven’t you?”
“I turned them all down. You don’t need to put yourself out there. Whether you save the world or destroy it, that isn’t what matters to those people.”
The distant sound of the loudspeaker.
I knew very well what my mother was worried about, and what she was sorry for.
“I’m not the Kim Dokja I was back then, either.”
When I drew back the curtain, every camera in the square swung toward the window.
Those cameras had frightened me once. I had been afraid of someone watching me, afraid of strangers talking about me in unfamiliar language.
“I’ll do the interview.”
“······Are you sure? Perhaps you should reconsider······.”
“They have a right to know, too.”
I turned the television back on. News headlines appeared on the screen.
―What is <Kim Dokja’s Company>’s objective?
―The [Industrial Complex] must reveal the nature of the final scenario······.
[Some nebulae are watching your movements!]
[The <Star Stream> wishes to tell your ‘Conclusion’!]
[The Great Dokkaebis are summoning you to the ‘final scenario’ area.]
[Some nebulae wish to form an alliance with your nebula······.]
“Eight tonight. Please contact the dokkaebis and constellations, too.”
For the first time in a while, I looked up the very first version of ‘Ways of Survival’ and read it.
The completely untouched ‘Ways of Survival’, before the author had made any revisions.
[You and your nebula are currently qualified for the ‘final scenario’.]
[You may enter the ‘final scenario’ area at any time.]
The final scenario in ‘Ways of Survival’ was an all-out war with the ‘Outer Gods’.
In that scenario, the original Yoo Joonghyuk beheaded the Outer God King and completed his ‘Conclusion’.
In a sense, it resembled the scenario we had already experienced through the ‘Great Apocalypse Scenario’.
In fact, had we failed to stop the Great Apocalypse, the Great Apocalypse would have become the preliminary battle for the final scenario.
「The ‘Outer Gods’ who should have become the disasters of the final scenario had been sealed.」
I looked at the three sealing spheres in the center of the [Factory].
All the ‘kings’ who had descended upon this worldline lay asleep inside.
‘The Living Flame’, ‘Master of the Sunken Island’, and ‘Monarch of the Great Abyss’.
Only the ‘King of the Silver Heart’, who had not descended as a disaster, remained unsealed.
―I will watch your Story to the end.

At the final moment, Uriel of the 999th round had said those words and sealed herself and her companions inside the [Apocalypse Dragon Sealing Spheres]. Having voluntarily broken her agreement with the Bureau and relinquished her rights as a disaster, she had sensed the tremendous repercussions that would follow.
[You ended the ‘Great Apocalypse Scenario’ in an abnormal manner.]
[Some constellations express dissatisfaction with the way you proceed through scenarios!]
[Some Great Dokkaebis harbor an unexplained hostility toward you.]
[A few Great Dokkaebis acknowledge your achievement in persuading the ‘Outer Gods’.]
[Many Wenny men currently regard you favorably.]
Countless message logs still drifted through the air.
[The hidden scenario ― ‘A Single Story’ is nearing completion.]
[You have completed a ‘Giant Story’ sufficient for the latter half of Conclusion (結).]
[The <Star Stream> proposes names for your final Story.]
[Choose a name for your Giant Story.]
[Your ‘Conclusion’ will be determined by the option you choose.]
I had yet to choose from the options the <Star Stream> had offered.
“Kim Dokja.”
The door creaked open, and Han Sooyoung appeared.
“How is everyone?”
“Same as before. Yoo Joonghyuk got hurt, but it wasn’t that serious. The [Life and Death Pill] really packs a punch.”
Uncharacteristically chatty, Han Sooyoung told me she had managed to get one more pill, then placed it in my hand.
“Take it if you think you’re going to croak.”
“I would have been more touched if you’d put it nicely.”
Han Sooyoung looked at my face with an unreadable gaze. A thin darkness hung between us like mist.
A faint light seeped from the sealing sphere holding Uriel of the 999th round.
In that light, Han Sooyoung’s face also glowed white.
“This really is the end now.”
I nodded.
“What was it like in the original? The final scenario······. No, never mind. It’ll be completely different from the original by now anyway.”
She was right.
We had already finished the war with the ‘Outer Gods’ that we should have faced in the original scenario.
The ‘final scenario’ we were to receive would probably be very different from the original.
“What happens when we complete our ‘Conclusion’?”
“We’ll probably meet the King of Stories.”
“The Dokkaebi King, you mean.”
Han Sooyoung thought for a moment before asking,
“Are you going to meet him?”
“I have to. Though not right away.”
“What’s that supposed to mean? You’re making me nervous.”
There came a knock, followed by a faint breeze.
One of the Industrial Complex’s members poked their head through the gap left when Han Sooyoung had opened the door.
“Representative-nim. You have a visitor.”
A visitor?
[It has been a long time, descendant.]
That archaic manner of speech. My visitor was someone entirely unexpected.
“······Pungbaek?”
The Heavenly Wind God, ‘Pungbaek’.
Come to think of it, I remembered what my mother had told me.
She had said to meet Pungbaek before entering the ‘final scenario’.
[Your choice was reckless, descendant. To let the ‘Outer Gods’ live—you have taken a disaster into your own arms.]
······Had he come to lecture me like an old fogey again?
As though nothing I did pleased him, Pungbaek launched into a lecture. Young people these days took scenarios too lightly, they weren’t serious enough about them······.
“Excuse me, Grandpa.”
[There is no time for a lengthy discussion, so I shall come to the point. You will face a great crisis in the final scenario, descendant.]
“A crisis?”
[I say this because I have watched your methods for a very long time.]
His tone suggested he could see exactly what I would do next. Han Sooyoung snickered beside me, seemingly amused. I shot her a glare, then asked,
“What exactly have you come to tell me?”
[<Hongik> can help you, descendant.]
My brow furrowed before I knew it. I thought I could see why he had come. This old man, right to the very end······.
“I don’t need it. You’ll obviously demand another ridiculous price······.”
[No price is necessary. Merely seeing a new ‘Myth-grade constellation’ born on the Korean Peninsula is payment enough.]
For a moment, I wondered if I had misheard.
[The Myth-grade constellations of the final scenario include <Hongik>’s creator gods. If things go poorly, ask them for help. If your appeal is sincere, they, too, will be compelled to act.]
“······You came to tell me that?”
Stroking his beard, Pungbaek answered expressionlessly,
[Indeed.]
“I’m a little touched.”
Pungbaek cleared his throat lightly, and his body scattered into the wind.
[I have said all I came to say. We shall meet in the final scenario.]
In an instant, only a chilly breeze remained. Han Sooyoung spoke, sounding surprised.
“What a coy old thing. He’s cute.”
“Well, he was a good constellation in the original.”
“You still have a few people on your side. Your life hasn’t been a complete waste.”
I hoped so.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ says she is here, too.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ insists that true companions are friends who lead one another astray (惡友)······.]
[The constellation ‘Most Ancient Liberator’······.]
I looked up at the sky and grinned. Han Sooyoung said,
“There’s that obnoxious grin again. It’s almost eight. Get ready. People are waiting.”
I nodded and headed to the upper floors of the [Factory]. Voices murmured inside. Every sort of news outlet, as well as dokkaebis and constellations, was waiting for me.
Just before I entered the press conference, a member of the Industrial Complex stopped me.
“Representative-nim, just a moment. We aren’t finished getting you ready.”
······Come to think of it, when had people in the [Industrial Complex] started calling me that?
I thought they used to call me Demon King.
“I told them to call you that. All that ‘Demon King-nim, Demon King-nim’ made us sound like the villains of the century.”
“Well, there’s that······. But Seolhwa-ssi, do we really have to do this?”
Seated before I quite knew what was happening, I twitched my lips as a brush tickled my cheek. Lee Seolhwa spoke as she painted my face with a serious expression.
“You are our representative, after all. We need to make you look human before sending you out.”
“That hurts in several different ways.”
Nearby, my companions watched as though something entertaining were happening. I felt like a monkey in a zoo.
Behind me, Han Sooyoung fiddled with my hair as she spoke.
“Is your hair going to stay blond, by the way?”
“It’s because of the Status that seeped into me from the Great Sage, Heaven’s Equal. The color will fade in a while.”
“Your hair’s really silky.”
[The constellation ‘Most Ancient Liberator’ says his hair has been honed through arduous training······.]
“Finished.”
Having finished coloring my face in no time, Lee Seolhwa held up a mirror.
I felt awkward saying so myself, but an incredibly handsome man was there—handsome enough to make me wonder whether I could give Yoo Joonghyuk a run for his money.
I glanced around, but none of my companions said anything.
A few paces away, Yoo Joonghyuk was glaring at me as though I were pathetic.
“Kim Dokja.”
I nodded. I put on my coat and buckled [Unbreakable Faith] to my waist. Apart from the suit underneath, it was my usual battle attire.
“Let’s go.”
We entered the press conference. Countless stars and cameras watched me from the wide-open outdoor venue.
Dazzling spotlights shone down from the sky. My companions and I were projected onto a huge holographic screen.
The citizens’ cheers. Amid the outpouring of cheers were the stories of those waiting for me.
[The overwhelming majority of constellations focus their attention on your choice!]
[The overwhelming majority of constellations are curious about the name of your final Story!]
Those concerned for the Korean Peninsula’s safety, constellations wondering whether Earth would survive.
Those who feared what awaited in the final scenario and worried about their own survival.
Beings who feared the power we possessed and sought to take it from us.
People asking why we had only appeared now, and incarnations demanding that we send all of them to the ‘final scenario’······.
[The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’ begins his story.]

Before the flood of questions, my Stories stirred. The sky rippled and the earth heaved. As the Status of a Myth-grade constellation was released, the entire Korean Peninsula fell silent. Everyone awaiting my answer was looking at me.
Slowly, I opened my mouth.
[Everyone.]
And began to speak.
[I have no intention of saving you.]
The crowd stirred at my declaration. Reporters kept snapping photos, and the low- and intermediate-grade dokkaebis reporting the situation on various channels looked appalled.
[Many constellations find your statement interesting!]
[The Great Dokkaebis listen closely to your statement.]
[Every dokkaebi in the <Bureau> is watching your words and actions!]
―What on earth do you mean?
―Representative Kim Dokja-nim!
Seeing constellations, incarnations, and dokkaebis all wearing the same expression was quite something.
With a kindly smile, I spoke again.
[I mean exactly what I said. I see no need to save you.]
―Are you saying you’ll abandon Korea?
―Then what about all the incarnations who supported you until now?
Supported me.
[How, exactly, did you support me?]

The uproar spread in an instant. My sly tone sent reporters springing to their feet and shouting over one another. The power of the press was impressive indeed, enough to resist the Status of a ‘Myth-grade constellation’.
―Who do you think tolerated <Kim Dokja’s Company>’s dictatorship?
―Haven’t we all followed your wishes until now?
Tolerated our dictatorship······.
Before I could react, the constellations did.
[Some constellations scoff at the reporters’ remarks.]
[The Korean Peninsula’s ancient constellations lament!]
[The constellation ‘Goryeo’s First Sword’ glares at his descendants.]
Leaving aside whether this was a dictatorship, I had no idea what they had ever tolerated. Even now, I heard there were protests against <Kim Dokja’s Company> every day in the ruins of Yeouido.
I gazed at the reporters shouting from every direction, then asked,
[And what are my wishes?]
[Have I ever asked you to do anything, even once?]

The reporters fell silent and looked at one another. The dokkaebis looked intrigued. To them, even this must have been an entertaining Story. A scene in which the ‘Demon King of Salvation’ abandoned his own land.
What rescued the momentarily flustered reporters was a group of incarnations waiting at one side of the [Industrial Complex].
―Great power inevitably carries duties. You have just thrown those duties to the ground.

An old man stepped forward abruptly and spoke, a shabby cap on his head. Sinister eyes gleamed beneath its bent brim. I couldn’t recall him immediately, but he was a supporting character from ‘Ways of Survival’. Behind me, I heard Lee Jihye.
“What? That old geezer came all the way here?”
Apparently, he belonged to the Busan alliance. While we were away from the Korean Peninsula, a new faction had taken control of the alliance.
Behind him were a veterans’ association flag and a group wearing blue headbands. Regional alliance members lined up on either side of them, raising their voices.
―Demon King of Salvation, you have the duties of the strong. Aren’t you the only ‘Myth-grade constellation’ active on the Korean Peninsula?
Some emphasized my duty.
―Please, do not abandon the Korean Peninsula! If you take that attitude, what are this land’s poor citizens supposed to do?
Others appealed to my sympathy.
―Face the final scenario with us! Everyone who has survived this far deserves a proper reward!
―None of these people wanted the ‘scenarios’! Will you abandon all these innocents? Can you still call yourself a constellation of the Korean Peninsula?
In a sense, they were right.
None of us had wanted the scenarios.
At first, that had been true.
[It’s fortunate that the alliance leaders are here, too.]
But was it still true now?
[There’s something I’d like to ask. Until the ‘final scenario’ arrived, where exactly were you, and what were you doing?]
The alliance members looked at one another.
―We······ protected the Korean Peninsula in your absence······!
―Are you dismissing the alliance’s hard work? We were the ones protecting the Korean Peninsula while you were away!
I knew what they would have been doing. I saw some of the alliance members exchange glances with the reporters.
「Run the article. The ‘Demon King of Salvation’ declares he’s abandoning the Korean Peninsula.」
They had probably been stirring up public opinion.
「‘Demon King of Salvation’ reveals his true demonic nature.」
Headlines that came to mind without my even having to ask.
I knew why they were going to such lengths.
「No need to be scared. The Demon King of Salvation is human, after all. He’s just a Korean.」
「As long as he was born here, there are things he can’t defy.」
「No matter how much power or fame he has······.」
They believed in the system. In the story called 「democracy」 that humanity had maintained for so long, or in Stories called 「rationalism」, 「institutions」, and 「majority rule」.
[Ancient Stories look at you.]

Now I could see them. Stories everyone believed they possessed, yet no one truly did. Even before the <Star Stream> arrived, Earth had been ruled by Giant Stories. And those who believed in those Stories would think they were right this time, too. The alliance members continued shouting.
―Wasn’t <Kim Dokja’s Company> the one monopolizing the scenarios in the first place? What could we do in such unfair competition?
[The ‘Industrial Complex’ has always been open. All the skills and Stories we obtained should have been made public.]
―But you entered the scenarios first······!
[Many people overseas entered the scenarios late. In Fei Hu’s and Ranveer Khan’s divisions, plenty of people who joined the scenarios only a few months ago have already reached the later scenarios.]
―That’s overseas! The situation here is different!
[They had no ‘Industrial Complex’. Support was concentrated on only a handful of people. But what about Seoul?]
I snapped my fingers, and Biyoo created a panel in the air. Footage of the [Industrial Complex]’s interior appeared on the enormous panel.

[We published strategies for the lower scenarios and lists of ‘Giant Story scenarios’. We did not hold back on special assistance for those who participated diligently in the scenarios. Gender, age, race—we placed no restrictions on any of them. What we wanted were people with the courage to fight alongside us.]
The screen showed incarnations training over and over. My mother directing them. I could also see Cho Youngran and Lee Boksoon working as instructors.
People who had completed that desperate training, earned Stories, and come here.
[I mean the people standing right before your eyes.]

The incarnations guarding the center of the press conference around me, with their sturdy bearing and mighty Status. They were the ‘wanderers’ my mother had raised. These were the heroes who had helped her stop the tidal wave in the East Sea.
[Has anyone here received less support than they did?]
No one answered. They had all been overwhelmed by the fierce spirit radiating from the ‘wanderers’ right in front of them.
People who had faltered and bitten their lips shouted,

―It’s not as if we were just fooling around! We were making all sorts of preparations. Improving institutions and facilities, and preparing to rebuild a proper nation once you finished the scenarios······.
[Why did you prepare for that? Do you know what ‘ending’ is coming?]
―What?
[Why do you think this world’s ‘ending’ will be peaceful?]
This world had changed greatly from the one in ‘Ways of Survival’. Yoo Joonghyuk, Lee Hyunsung, Lee Jihye, Shin Yoosung. All of them were a little different from the people I had known.
But some things had not changed.
「Everyone Yoo Joonghyuk met wished, without exception, for everything to return to the way it had been.」
Bewilderment spread across their faces. Faces betrayed by the hope they had trusted to the very end. I knew very well what they wanted.
「Yet none of them truly wished for ‘everything’ to return to the way it had been.」
What the crowd wanted was not peace for everyone, but ‘their own peace’.
They had certainly endured hellish scenarios and survived. And people who had endured such scenarios never wanted everything to go ‘back to normal’.
Because even the hell they had endured was now their story.
「······The final scenario just needs to end. I have power now, too. At least among the incarnations, I can finally be the one on top.」
「I can’t go back to the old days. Not after everything I went through to survive······.」
「If only <Kim Dokja’s Company> weren’t here······.」
Amid those countless seething desires, I slowly turned to look at the edge of the press conference.
Beyond the alliance members and reporters were people looking up at me. Ordinary incarnations in grubby clothes and equipment, dust covering their bodies.

I saw a little girl, too. About as tall as Shin Yoosung had been in the early scenarios. So young that her survival seemed miraculous. There, where cameras and channels alike looked away, the girl murmured to herself in a voice only I could hear.
「Then······ are we all going to die now?」
Amid the torrent of clicking shutters, I looked at that young girl for a long time.
Then I spoke.
[I am no hero. I never intended to save all of you, and I have no plans to do so. But―]
When I slowly turned around,
[The other ‘representative’ may think differently.]
Yoo Joonghyuk was there.
A little later, Han Sooyoung and I were listening to Yoo Joonghyuk’s speech from backstage.
―I do not know what ending he envisions. But I, too, have an ending in mind for this world.
Normally, the most he said was something like “I’ll kill you, Kim Dokja,” but once he started talking, he could give a decent speech. Yoo Joonghyuk wasn’t the protagonist for nothing.
Han Sooyoung, gazing at me with a lemon candy in her mouth. As though making excuses, I said,
“I can’t stay in the spotlight and control everything forever. Yoo Joonghyuk is better suited to that sort of thing. He was in the original, too.”
Han Sooyoung chuckled, and I added,
“They need a firmer rallying point. That isn’t my role.”
“You could have done it.”
“It’s time I went back to where I belong. I’m a reader, not the protagonist.”
“Oh, really? Now, of all times?”

Hiding my hands behind my back, I clenched and unclenched my fists. Apparently, Kim Dokja was still Kim Dokja even after becoming a constellation. My palms were damp with sweat. Standing before cameras was never easy.
“Is that your idea of a ‘proper ending’?”
“It’s the beginning of one.”
“What comes next?”
I didn’t answer.
“Hey.”
Han Sooyoung strode over, rose onto her toes, and grabbed me by the collar.
“You haven’t forgotten you promised to read my novel, have you?”
“Huh?”
“You promised. Did you forget?”
Looking into her burning eyes, I remembered conversations we had once had.
That was right. As we left the ‘Kaizenix Archipelago’, Han Sooyoung had said it.
That she wanted to write a novel once all these scenarios were over.
And that she wanted me to read her novel then.
“You were serious about that?”
“Would I lie about something like that?”
I smiled wryly.
“I’m a pretty demanding reader. Are you sure you’re up for it?”
“A demanding reader spent ten years reading something like Ways of Survival?”
“I might leave nasty comments. I might point out that something’s implausible, or comment that I’m dropping it.”
“Try it. See what happens.”
I studied Han Sooyoung’s face. That unyielding gaze, meeting mine without retreating an inch. That was right. This was who Han Sooyoung had always been.
“······I might pester you to release extra chapters every day.”
“No problem. I’ve written ten installments a day before.”

As we bickered with her hand still gripping my collar, everything somehow began to feel unreal. When I had first seen her, I had never imagined we would become companions. Han Sooyoung. The person who had been the ‘King of the Prophets’.
―There was a time when I distinguished between people I had to save and people I could let die.
Yoo Joonghyuk’s voice reached us.
―Some must die, and others must live. I lived my life thinking that way. I believed it was necessary for this world. But now······.

Listening to that speech, Han Sooyoung and I stopped talking. Yoo Joonghyuk’s innermost thoughts, which he had never spoken aloud. We listened to the inner self that even ‘Ways of Survival’ had never fully revealed.
―Now, I am not sure.
The protagonist of ‘Ways of Survival’ was speaking.
Behind him flowed the Stories of the round we had lived through.
The one being in this world who did not forget the worlds that had passed.
The protagonist who had been betrayed and wounded in the distant past.
―I have received help from someone I believed to be evil in a previous life.
I saw Yoo Joonghyuk fighting Asmodeus.
Yoo Joonghyuk meeting his death after a fierce battle in the second round.
―And I have fought once more on the same front as someone who betrayed me.
Anna Croft helping us face the Apocalypse Dragon.
Yoo Joonghyuk watched those Stories for a long time before continuing.
―I have not forgiven them. But neither do I intend to use this life to take revenge on them. Because this life is not my previous life. Just as this world is no longer the world you once knew.
People were listening to Yoo Joonghyuk’s story.
They were neither regressors nor protagonists. And yet their faces suggested they might understand something.

―Surviving does not mean everything is permitted to you. On the contrary, you bear a responsibility. The sin of surviving. The sin of surviving by trampling others’ stories. The sin of daring to put forth stems and shoots, using others’ Stories as fertilizer. So if you have survived, take responsibility for that sin.
Those who understood and those who did not all looked overwhelmed.
The words of a human who had lived on the front lines of the scenarios, cutting down constellations.
They were neither kindly consolation nor warm encouragement, but they reached people clearly.
His voice held far more sincerity than the True Voice of a constellation like me.
―I cannot promise to save everyone. I can only live through my own scenario. I cannot live your scenarios for you. So there is only one thing I want to tell you.
That was where Yoo Joonghyuk belonged.
―Until all your scenarios have ended, I, too, will neither die nor regress.
The crowd fell silent at Yoo Joonghyuk’s tremendous declaration.
A few alliance members unmoved by his eloquence exchanged glances, but the crowd’s fervor was already beyond their control.
“Supreme King······.”
Someone murmured, and the reporters began inventing headlines of their own.
「Supreme King Yoo Joonghyuk declares he will fight to the death!」
「Yoo Joonghyuk, joint representative of <Kim Dokja’s Company>: “I will not give up on the scenarios until the very end.”」
Incarnations who had heard the rumors that he was a regressor seemed even more excited. Someone shouted loudly, and the [Factory] was engulfed in cheers in an instant.
“Supreme King Yoo Joonghyuk!”
“Yoo Joonghyuk! Yoo Joonghyuk!”
